# Hooks

A hook is raised before the operation it names, and delivered at once: a handler may change the fields listed as changeable, with `modify` or `set`, or stop the operation with `cancel_event` (05 §8.2). Every event also binds `actor` and `instigator` from its cause where the cause names them.

<a id="ability-granting"></a>
## `ability_granting`

Runs before a rule grants an ability (`grant_ability`; 08 §12). A handler may cancel, with a reason: a gift that cannot be given.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `source` (string): What gives it: `rule`.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="ability-revoking"></a>
## `ability_revoking`

Runs before a rule revokes an ability (`revoke_ability`; 08 §12). A handler may cancel, with a reason: a gift that cannot be stolen.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="ability-using"></a>
## `ability_using`

Runs before a granted action is started through its ability (08 §7.9), after the ability was found usable. A handler may change the parameters and the cost for this use, or cancel, with a reason.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action.
- `params` (any): The action's parameters, by name: what the command gave and the grant's `params`. A handler may change them; each is held to its type again.
- `cost` (any): The cost by pool or item, a map of qualified id to amount. A handler may change an amount, to zero or more, for this use only.

A handler may change `params`, `cost`, or cancel.

<a id="action-starting"></a>
## `action_starting`

Runs before an action claims its channels and enters its first phase. A handler may change its parameters, or cancel with a reason, which is what whoever asked is told; with none, `engine:action_vetoed`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `params` (any): The action's parameters by name, as a map, defaults filled in. Mutable: a value a handler puts there is held to the parameter's type, and one that does not fit refuses the action.

A handler may change `params`, or cancel.

<a id="body-changing"></a>
## `body_changing`

Runs before a body is edited by a verb of 06 §6.5 that reshapes it. A handler may cancel, with a reason: a body that cannot be reshaped.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `verb` (string): Which edit, as `body_changed` names it.
- `part` (string): The name of the part to be edited, or of the part a new one is to go on; empty for an edit of the whole body.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="defence-resolving"></a>
## `defence_resolving`

Runs before a defence of `self` in force is applied to a strike by `attacker` at `target` (07 §5, step 5 of 07 §3.4). A handler may change how much it turns (`deflect`, `holds`), what it braces, or make it fail (`succeeded` false, or cancel).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `attacker` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the defending action.
- `form` (string): `avoid` or `interpose`.
- `succeeded` (bool): Whether it succeeds: its contest's margin was at or above zero, or it has none.
- `margin` (real?): The margin of its contest; null for a defence with none.
- `deflect` (real): The share of the strike's energy it turns aside, 0 to 1.
- `holds` (real?): The most joules it can turn aside; null for no limit.
- `brace` (real): The share of the push it resists, 0 to 1.

A handler may change `succeeded`, `deflect`, `holds`, `brace`, or cancel.

<a id="entity-dying"></a>
## `entity_dying`

Runs before an entity stops for good (06 §8.3). A handler may cancel: the entity then goes on.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="exposure-incoming"></a>
## `exposure_incoming`

Runs before a dose reaches a body by any route (02 §16). A handler may change the amount, which is how a mask keeps part of it out, or cancel it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `pool` (id<pool>): The pool the dose adds to.
- `amount` (real): The dose.
- `route` (string): The route it takes: `breath`, `skin` or `any`.
- `field` (string): The field it comes from: the qualified id of a `field`.

A handler may change `amount`, or cancel.

<a id="hit-incoming"></a>
## `hit_incoming`

Runs before a hit is applied to a body (06 §7.1). A handler may change its energy, its intensity, the part it lands on and its direction, or cancel it. `actor` and `instigator` are whoever is behind the hit.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part?): The part the hit is aimed at. Null for a hit at a height, anywhere, or spread over the body.
- `height` (real?): The height above the target's footing it arrives at, in metres, for a hit aimed at a height.
- `spread` (bool): Whether it is spread over the whole body.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `energy` (real): Joules delivered.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated the delivery is, in pascals.
- `area` (real): The area of contact, in square metres.
- `span` (real): The length of contact across the part, in metres.
- `dir` (list<real>?): The direction it travels in: east, south and up.

A handler may change `energy`, `intensity`, `part`, `dir`, or cancel.

<a id="interaction-reach"></a>
## `interaction_reach`

Runs when reach is tested for an attempt at an interaction (16 §3.3): `self` the user; `target` the entity, or `element` the element, it is done to. A handler may set `reached` to extend reach (telekinesis, a long tongue) or deny it. Not raised by a listing of what is offered.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `element` (element).

Fields:

- `interaction` (string): The qualified id of the interaction.
- `reach` (string): The interaction's reach: `held`, `same_cell`, `adjacent`, `range` or `network`.
- `reached` (bool): Whether the user reaches the target. Mutable.

A handler may change `reached`, or cancel.

<a id="interaction-starting"></a>
## `interaction_starting`

Runs before an interaction begins (16 §3.4), once reach and `if` have held. A handler may cancel with a reason, which is what the user is told: a lock, an alarm, a permission, a trap.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `element` (element).

Fields:

- `interaction` (string): The qualified id of the interaction.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="item-leaving"></a>
## `item_leaving`

Runs before a thing leaves the hold it is in, with `holder` what holds it now. A handler may cancel: a thing that will not come off. Not raised when a part that can no longer hold lets go, nor when the holder is removed.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `holder` (entity).

Fields:

- `hold` (string): The kind of hold: `grasp`, `worn`, `stowed`, `seat`, `inside` or `fixed`.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="item-taking"></a>
## `item_taking`

Runs before a thing enters a hold: a grasp, being worn, a container. A handler may cancel: a thing that will not be picked up. Not raised for a thing put somewhere by the kernel's `relocate` alone.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `holder` (entity).

Fields:

- `hold` (string): The kind of hold: `grasp`, `worn`, `stowed`, `seat`, `inside` or `fixed`.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="knockback-incoming"></a>
## `knockback_incoming`

Runs before a push moves `self` (07 §7). A handler may change the speed and the direction, or cancel: nothing moves it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `speed` (real): The speed the push gives, in metres a second.
- `dir` (list<real>): Its direction: east, south, up, of length one.

A handler may change `speed`, `dir`, or cancel.

<a id="mind-transferring"></a>
## `mind_transferring`

Runs before a mind is moved from `self` to `target`, and before `self` is given a driver (06 §8.2). A handler may cancel.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `swap` (bool): Whether the two minds are to change places.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="passage-requested"></a>
## `passage_requested`

Runs when a mover (`self`) would step into the cell `here` that `target` fills (06 §11). A handler sets `yields` to true to make the two change places; cancelling, or leaving it false, refuses the step.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `yields` (bool): Whether `target` lets the mover by. False until a handler sets it.

A handler may change `yields`, or cancel.

<a id="phase-timing"></a>
## `phase_timing`

Runs before a phase that has a duration is scheduled. A handler may change the duration. Cancelling it changes nothing: the phase is scheduled as it was.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.
- `phase` (string): The id of the phase.
- `duration` (real): How long the phase is to last, in seconds of the actor's own clock, after tempo. Mutable; a value below zero counts as zero.

A handler may change `duration`, or cancel.

<a id="pool-changing"></a>
## `pool_changing`

Runs before a verb changes a pool's level. A handler may change the amount or cancel. Rates and regeneration do not raise it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `pool` (id<pool>): The pool.
- `amount` (real): What is about to be added; negative to take away.

A handler may change `amount`, or cancel.

<a id="posture-changing"></a>
## `posture_changing`

Runs before an entity's posture changes (06 §11.1). A handler may cancel: the posture stays.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `from` (string): The qualified id of the posture it is in; empty for none.
- `to` (string): The qualified id of the posture it would take; empty for none.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.

<a id="scenario-ending"></a>
## `scenario_ending`

Runs before an ending takes effect (13 §9.4). A handler may change `as`, or cancel: the game goes on.

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `as` (string): The outcome the ending names. A handler may change it.

A handler may change `as`, or cancel.

<a id="strike-resolving"></a>
## `strike_resolving`

Runs before a strike by `self` is resolved (07 §3.4, step 1). A handler may change whom it strikes, the part it is aimed at, its energy and its effort, or cancel: nothing is struck and the action's `$landed` stays false.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action whose attack it is.
- `attack` (string): The id of the attack within it.
- `target` (entity?): Whom it strikes; null for a strike at a cell.
- `part` (part?): The part of the target it is aimed at, if one is.
- `energy` (real): Joules at full effort: what the attack's `energy` gave.
- `effort` (real): The share of that put into it, 0 to 1.

A handler may change `target`, `part`, `energy`, `effort`, or cancel.

<a id="trait-adding"></a>
## `trait_adding`

Runs before an entity is given a trait (06 §5), whether it is new to it, refreshed or stacked. A handler may cancel, with a reason, and may change `duration`. Not raised when giving it would change nothing.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `trait` (string): The qualified id of the trait.
- `giver` (string): What gave it: `rule`, `item`, `posture`, `ability`, `template` or `other`.
- `stacks` (int): How many stacks the instance will have.
- `duration` (real?): How long it will last, in seconds of the holder's time, or null for one that lasts until removed. A handler may change it: a number above zero, or null.

A handler may change `duration`, or cancel.

<a id="trait-removing"></a>
## `trait_removing`

Runs before `remove_trait` removes a trait or some of its stacks (06 §5). A handler may cancel, with a reason. Not raised when a trait expires, is replaced by one of its group, or is withdrawn by what gave it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `trait` (string): The qualified id of the trait.
- `stacks` (int): How many stacks would go, over every giver.

A handler may change no field; it may cancel.
